```{r}
#** --- Set up a valid path --- *
# Define base paths for both possible directories
base_paths <- c(
  "E:/OneDrive/TUNCOM/TUNCRG/06. Phase 2 Data/Aging",
  "C:/Users/samue/OneDrive/TUNCOM/TUNCRG/06. Phase 2 Data/Aging"
)

# Find the first existing directory
valid_path <- first(base_paths[dir.exists(base_paths)])

if (is.na(valid_path)) {
  stop("Neither of the specified base directories exists. Please check the paths.")
}

#** --- Define objects to keep --- *
# This list helps in managing the global environment
CoreDatasets <- c(
"CorsanoAnalysismulti", "CorsanoAnalysissingle", "CorsanoAnalysisSleepexpand", "SleepAnalysis", "StatS", "CoreDatasets", "subjects", "SplitModel2", "Statistics", "biomarkers", "SleepStat", "Analysis", "CorsanoAnalysissplit", "valid_path", "processed_subjects", "Stat", "processed_subjects1", "processed_subjects2", "processed_subjects3", "CorsanoAnalysisAll", "Shiftwork", "Shiftwork2", "ShiftStat", "Sleepwork", "CorsanoAnalysisSleepmulti", "CorsanoAnalysisSleepsingle", "CorsanoAnalysisWave", "PhaseDiff", "SLEEP", "CorsanoShiftWave", "Variability", "Stability", "SJL", "StatSS", "SLEEP1", "AmpMesAge", "AmpMesGen", "BioBmiStats", "DeviationsS", "SJLDeviations", "SJLBIO", "jsl_summary", "Jetlag", "biolist", "PhysCog", "Aging", "AgingA", "SJL2", "SJLBio"
```

#**================================================================**
#** CORE PROCESSING CODE                                           **
#**================================================================**
```{r}

#**================================================================**
#** 2. Helper Functions                                            **
#**================================================================**

#' Replace NaN and NULL values with NA.
#' @param x A vector or column.
#' @return A vector with NaN/NULL replaced by NA.
replace_nan_with_NA <- function(x) {
  if(is.null(x)) {
    return(NA)
  } else {
    x[is.nan(x)] <- NA
    return(x)
  }
}

#' Summarize biomarker data by specified grouping variables.
#' Matches the logic of explicitly writing out mean/SEM for every variable.
#' ROBUST VERSION: Checks for existence of columns before processing.
#' @param data A dataframe.
#' @param group_vars A character vector of column names to group by.
#' @return A summarized and ungrouped dataframe.
summarize_biomarkers <- function(data, group_vars) {
  
  # Identify standard biomarkers (excluding Energy) that ACTUALLY exist in the data
  available_cols <- names(data)
  std_bios <- intersect(biolist[biolist != "Energy"], available_cols)
  
  # 1. Base summary for standard biomarkers
  res <- data %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) %>%
    summarise(
      across(
        all_of(std_bios),
        list(
          mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          SEM = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.x)))
        ),
        .names = "{.col}{.fn}" # Output names like HRmean, HRSEM
      ),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # 2. Special handling for Energy (only if it exists in data)
  if ("Energy" %in% available_cols) {
    energy_res <- data %>%
      group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) %>%
      summarise(
        Energy_mean = mean(Energy[Energy != 0], na.rm = TRUE),
        Energy_SEM = sd(Energy[Energy != 0], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(Energy[Energy != 0]))),
        .groups = 'drop'
      )
    # Join Energy results back to main result
    res <- left_join(res, energy_res, by = group_vars)
  }
  
  # 3. Clean up column names
  res %>%
    rename_with(~sub("_mean$", "", .), ends_with("_mean")) %>%
    rename_with(~sub("_SEM$", "SEM", .), ends_with("_SEM"))
}

#**================================================================**
#** 3. Data Preparation & Aggregation                              **
#**================================================================**

# --- Prepare Weekday/Weekend Split ---
CorsanoAnalysissplit <- CorsanoAnalysismulti %>%
  mutate(Week = ifelse(Day %in% c("Saturday", "Sunday"), "Weekend", "Weekday")) %>%
  # Convert and merge into 24-hour format, kept within the same day
  mutate(Time = Time %% 24,
         Time = trunc(Time * 1000) / 1000) %>%
  arrange(Subject, Week, Time)

# Duplicate rows where Time == 0, change Time to 24, and add them back
# This ensures continuous plotting at the midnight crossover
CorsanoAnalysissplit <- CorsanoAnalysissplit %>%
  bind_rows(CorsanoAnalysissplit %>%
              filter(Time == 0) %>%
              mutate(Time = 24)) %>%
  arrange(Subject, Week, Time)

# --- Create Aggregated Datasets using Helper Function ---

# 1. Combined by Weekday/Weekend
CorsanoAnalysisCombined <- summarize_biomarkers(CorsanoAnalysissplit, c("Time", "Subject", "Week")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Subject, Week, Time)

# 2. Combined for the whole week (Both)
# We calculate this from the source multi data to ensure correct weighting
CorsanoAnalysisBoth <- CorsanoAnalysismulti %>%
  mutate(Time = Time %% 24,
         Time = trunc(Time * 1000) / 1000) %>%
  select(-Day) %>%
  # Use the helper function here too, just grouping by Subject and Time
  summarize_biomarkers(c("Time", "Subject")) %>%
  mutate(Week = "Both") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Subject, Time)

# --- Final Cleanup and Combination ---
# Apply replace_nan_with_NA to all datasets
CorsanoAnalysissplit <- CorsanoAnalysissplit %>% mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA))
CorsanoAnalysisCombined <- CorsanoAnalysisCombined %>% mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA))
CorsanoAnalysisBoth <- CorsanoAnalysisBoth %>% mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA))

# Ensure Both dataset has correct column order before binding
CorsanoAnalysisBoth <- CorsanoAnalysisBoth %>%
  select(Time, Subject, Week, everything())

# Create Final Combined Dataset
CorsanoAnalysisAll <- bind_rows(CorsanoAnalysisBoth, CorsanoAnalysisCombined) %>%
  arrange(Subject, Time)

# --- Export Processed Data ---
file_paths <- c("CorsanoAnalysissplit", "CorsanoAnalysisAll")

if (!is.null(valid_path)) {
  for (file_name in file_paths) {
    write.xlsx(get(file_name), file.path(valid_path, "Outputs", paste0(file_name, ".xlsx")), rowNames = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  stop("valid_path is not defined.")
}



#**================================================================**
#** 4. Main Cosinor Analysis & Statistics Calculation Loop         **
#**================================================================**

# --- Initialization ---
# biolist is already defined in Section 1

# Define subjects to process, excluding any already completed
subjectnames <- unique(CorsanoAnalysissplit$Subject)

# Use one 'processed_subjects' list for simplicity
if (!exists("processed_subjects1")) processed_subjects1 <- character()
subjectnames <- setdiff(subjectnames, processed_subjects1)

# Initialize lists to store results efficiently
CorsanoAnalysisWave_list <- list()
Stattmp_list <- list()

# --- Main Processing Loop ---
for (subject in subjectnames) {
  cat("Processing Patient:", subject, "\n")
  
  # Create subject-specific output folder
  subject_folder <- file.path(valid_path, "Graphs", subject)
  if (!dir.exists(subject_folder)) {
    dir.create(subject_folder, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Process for "Weekday", "Weekend", and "Both"
  weekz <- c("Weekday", "Weekend", "Both")
  
  for (dayz in weekz) {
    cat("  Processing period:", dayz, "\n")
    
    # Filter data for the current analysis scope
    if (dayz == "Both") {
      GLMMSplit <- filter(CorsanoAnalysissplit, Subject == subject)
    } else {
      GLMMSplit <- filter(CorsanoAnalysissplit, Subject == subject, Week == dayz)
    }
    
    # Skip if there's insufficient data
    if (nrow(GLMMSplit) < 70) {
      cat("    Skipping due to insufficient data (", nrow(GLMMSplit), " rows).\n")
      next
    }
    
    # Initialize Wavedatatmp for this period
    Wavedatatmp <- data.frame()
    
    # --- Loop through each biomarker to perform cosinor analysis ---
    for (bio in biolist) {
      # cat("    Processing biometric:", bio, "\n")
      
      # 1. CHECK IF COLUMN EXISTS
      if (!bio %in% names(GLMMSplit)) {
        # cat("    Skipping", bio, "- column not found in data.\n")
        next
      }
      
      # 2. Ensure the biomarker column has enough data
      if (sum(!is.na(GLMMSplit[[bio]])) < 10) next
      
      # Run GLMM Cosinor Analysis (wrapped in tryCatch to handle model errors)
      model_formula <- as.formula(paste(bio, "~ amp_acro(time_col = 'Time', period = c(24, 12), n_components = 2)"))
      
      SplitModel2 <- tryCatch({
        cglmm(model_formula, data = GLMMSplit)
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("    ERROR fitting model for", bio, ":", e$message, "\n")
        return(NULL)
      })
      
      if (is.null(SplitModel2)) next
      
      # --- Generate predictions and summarize ---
      prediction <- predict(SplitModel2, GLMMSplit)
      Wavedatatmp1 <- GLMMSplit[, c("Time", bio)]
      Wavedatatmp1[[paste0(bio, "Cosine")]] <- prediction
      
      # Summarize raw data and cosine predictions
      Wavedatatmp1 <- Wavedatatmp1 %>%
        group_by(Time) %>%
        summarise(
          !!paste0(bio, "SEM") := sd(!!sym(bio), na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(!!sym(bio)))),
          !!paste0(bio) := mean(!!sym(bio), na.rm = TRUE),
          !!paste0(bio, "Cosine") := mean(!!sym(paste0(bio, "Cosine")), na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = 'drop'
        )
      
      # Join this biomarker's results to the cumulative data frame (Wavedatatmp)
      if (nrow(Wavedatatmp) == 0) {
        Wavedatatmp <- Wavedatatmp1  # If it's the first biomarker, directly assign
      } else {
        Wavedatatmp <- left_join(Wavedatatmp, Wavedatatmp1, by = "Time")  # Add new columns
      }
      
    } # End biomarker loop
    
    # --- Proceed if we have data ---
    if (nrow(Wavedatatmp) > 0) {
      
      # Create Double graph (48 hour view) - STRICTLY FOLLOWING ORIGINAL LOGIC
      Wavedatatmp2 <- Wavedatatmp %>%
        mutate(Time = Time + 24) %>%
        filter(Time != 24)
      
      Wavedata <- bind_rows(Wavedatatmp, Wavedatatmp2)
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------------------
      # ENFORCE EXACT COLUMN ORDER FOR TEMPLATE COMPATIBILITY
      # -----------------------------------------------------------------
      
      # Define the strict column order requested
      desired_columns <- c("Time", 
                           "CBT", "CBTCosine", "CBTSEM", 
                           "HR", "HRCosine", "HRSEM", 
                           "Breath", "BreathCosine", "BreathSEM", 
                           "HRV", "HRVCosine", "HRVSEM", 
                           "RR", "RRCosine", "RRSEM", 
                           "Cortisol", "CortisolCosine", "CortisolSEM", 
                           "Stress", "StressCosine", "StressSEM", 
                           "SBT", "SBTCosine", "SBTSEM", 
                           "Steps", "StepsCosine", "StepsSEM", 
                           "Energy", "EnergyCosine", "EnergySEM")
      
      # 1. Identify which columns from the desired list are missing in Wavedata
      missing_cols <- setdiff(desired_columns, names(Wavedata))
      
      # 2. Add missing columns with NA values (preserves structure for template)
      if(length(missing_cols) > 0) {
        Wavedata[missing_cols] <- NA
      }
      
      # 3. Select exactly the desired columns in the desired order
      Wavedata <- Wavedata %>%
        select(all_of(desired_columns)) %>%
        # Replace all NaN with NA one last time to be safe
        mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA))
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------------------
      
      # --- Export raw Wave data to Excel ---
      export_path <- file.path(subject_folder, paste0(subject, "_", dayz, "_Wave.xlsx"))
      write.xlsx(Wavedata, export_path, rowNames = FALSE, firstRow = TRUE)
      
      # =================================================================
      # GRAPHING TEMPLATE LOGIC - UPDATED & DEBUGGED
      # =================================================================
      
      if (dayz %in% c("Weekday", "Weekend")) {
        # Logic for Weekday/Weekend Split
        Template <- file.path(valid_path, "Graphing Template.xlsx")
        Graph <- file.path(subject_folder, paste0(subject, ".xlsx"))
        
        # 1. Creation Step: Copy Template if Graph file does not exist
        if (!file.exists(Graph)) {
          if (file.exists(Template)) {
            tryCatch({
              file.copy(from = Template, to = Graph, overwrite = FALSE)
              cat("    CREATED new graph file from Template for:", subject, "\n")
            }, error = function(e) {
              cat("    ERROR copying template:", e$message, "\n")
            })
          } else {
            cat("    WARNING: Template NOT found at:", Template, "\n")
          }
        }
        
        # 2. Writing Step: Open Workbook and write data if file exists
        if (file.exists(Graph)) {
          tryCatch({
            wb <- loadWorkbook(Graph)
            writeData(wb, sheet = dayz, x = Wavedata)
            saveWorkbook(wb, Graph, overwrite = TRUE)
            cat("    Success: Written data to sheet", dayz, "in", basename(Graph), "\n")
          }, error = function(e) {
            cat("    ERROR writing to graph file:", e$message, "\n")
          })
        } else {
          cat("    ERROR: Graph file could not be created or found at:", Graph, "\n")
        }
        
      } else if (dayz == "Both") {
        # Logic for "Both" (Combined Everyday)
        Template <- file.path(valid_path, "Graphing Template 2.xlsx")
        Graph <- file.path(subject_folder, paste0(subject, "All.xlsx"))
        
        # 1. Creation Step: Remove existing and start fresh
        if (file.exists(Graph)) {
          file.remove(Graph)
        }
        
        if (file.exists(Template)) {
          tryCatch({
            file.copy(from = Template, to = Graph, overwrite = TRUE)
            
            # 2. Writing Step
            if (file.exists(Graph)) {
              wb <- loadWorkbook(Graph)
              writeData(wb, sheet = "Raw", x = Wavedata)
              saveWorkbook(wb, Graph, overwrite = TRUE)
              cat("    Success: Created and updated 'All' graph file for:", subject, "\n")
            }
          }, error = function(e) {
             cat("    ERROR processing 'Both' file:", e$message, "\n")
          })
        } else {
          cat("    WARNING: Graphing Template 2.xlsx NOT found at:", Template, "\n")
        }
      }
      
      # =================================================================
      # END GRAPHING TEMPLATE LOGIC
      # =================================================================
      
      # --- Calculate Statistics (Min, Max, Amp, Mesor, etc.) ---
      cosine_data <- select(Wavedata, Time, ends_with("Cosine"))
      
      for (bio in biolist) {
        col_name <- paste0(bio, "Cosine")
        
        # Check if the column exists and is not all NA (since we forced cols to exist now)
        if (!col_name %in% names(cosine_data)) next
        vec <- cosine_data[[col_name]]
        if(all(is.na(vec))) next
        
        max_val <- max(vec, na.rm = TRUE)
        min_val <- min(vec, na.rm = TRUE)
        
        test_long <- data.frame(
          Patient = subject,
          week = dayz,
          Bio = bio,
          Amplitude = (max_val - min_val) / 2,
          Mesor = mean(vec, na.rm = TRUE),
          PPhase = cosine_data$Time[which.max(vec)],
          TPhase = cosine_data$Time[which.min(vec)],
          Max = max_val,
          Min = min_val
        )
        Stattmp_list[[length(Stattmp_list) + 1]] <- test_long
      }
      
      # Append collected wave data to the main list
      Wavedatatmp3 <- cosine_data %>%
        mutate(Subject = subject, Week = dayz)
      CorsanoAnalysisWave_list[[length(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list) + 1]] <- Wavedatatmp3
    }
    
  } # End dayz loop
  
  # Add subject to processed list after all its periods are complete
  processed_subjects1 <- c(processed_subjects1, subject)
  
} # End subject loop

#**================================================================**
#** 5. Final Aggregation and Export of Statistics                  **
#**================================================================**

# Combine all results from the lists at once for maximum efficiency
if (length(Stattmp_list) > 0) {
  Stattmp <- bind_rows(Stattmp_list)
  
  # Bind with any existing Stat data
  if(exists("Stat") && is.data.frame(Stat)) {
    Stat <- bind_rows(Stat, Stattmp)
  } else {
    Stat <- Stattmp
  }
  
  # Load and join patient demographic data if it exists
  patient_info_path <- file.path(valid_path, "Documentations", "patients.xlsx")
  if (file.exists(patient_info_path)) {
    PT <- read.xlsx(patient_info_path)
    Stat <- left_join(Stat, PT, by = c("Patient" = "Patient.Code"))
  }
  
  # Final arrangement and export
  Stat <- Stat %>%
    select(any_of(c("BMI", "week", "Bio", "Patient", "gender", "age")), everything()) %>%
    filter(Patient != "S5U469YF") %>%
    distinct()
  
  
  export_path <- file.path(valid_path, "Stats", "Full_Statistics_Optimized.xlsx")
  write.xlsx(Stat, export_path, rowNames = FALSE)
  cat("Statistical analysis complete. Results saved to:", export_path, "\n")
}

if (length(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list) > 0) {
  CorsanoAnalysisWave <- bind_rows(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list)
}

# Final cleanup
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), CoreDatasets))
```

```{r}
#**================================================================**
#** 2. Helper Functions                                           **
#**================================================================**

#' Replace NaN and NULL values with NA.
#' @param x A vector or column.
#' @return A vector with NaN/NULL replaced by NA.
replace_nan_with_NA <- function(x) {
  x[is.nan(x) | is.null(x)] <- NA
  return(x)
}


#' Summarize biomarker data by specified grouping variables.
#' This function replaces the repetitive summarise blocks.
#' @param data A dataframe.
#' @param group_vars A character vector of column names to group by.
#' @return A summarized and ungrouped dataframe.
summarize_biomarkers <- function(data, group_vars) {
  data %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) %>%
    summarise(
      # Process all biomarkers except for 'Energy' which has special handling
      across(
        all_of(biolist[biolist != "Energy"]),
        list(
          mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
          SEM = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.x)))
        ),
        .names = "{.col}{.fn}"
      ),
      # Special handling for Energy (excluding zeros)
      Energy_mean = mean(Energy[Energy != 0], na.rm = TRUE),
      Energy_SEM = sd(Energy[Energy != 0], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(Energy[Energy != 0]))),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    # Rename columns to match original format (e.g., HR_mean -> HR, HR_SEM -> HRSEM)
    rename_with(~sub("_mean$", "", .), ends_with("_mean")) %>%
    rename_with(~sub("_SEM$", "SEM", .), ends_with("_SEM"))
}


#**================================================================**
#** 3. Data Preparation & Aggregation                             **
#**================================================================**

# --- Prepare Weekday/Weekend Split ---
CorsanoAnalysissplit <- CorsanoAnalysismulti %>%
  mutate(
    Week = ifelse(Day %in% c("Saturday", "Sunday"), "Weekend", "Weekday"),
    Time = (Time %% 24), # Ensure time is within a 24-hour cycle
    Time = trunc(Time * 1000) / 1000
  ) %>%
  # Duplicate rows at Time == 0 and set them to Time = 24 for continuous plotting
  bind_rows(filter(., Time == 0) %>% mutate(Time = 24)) %>%
  arrange(Subject, Week, Time)

# --- Create Aggregated Datasets using the helper function ---
# Combined by Weekday/Weekend
CorsanoAnalysisCombined <- summarize_biomarkers(CorsanoAnalysissplit, c("Time", "Subject", "Week"))

# Combined for the whole week (Both)
CorsanoAnalysisBoth <- summarize_biomarkers(CorsanoAnalysissplit, c("Time", "Subject")) %>%
  mutate(Week = "Both")

# --- Final Cleanup and Combination ---
CorsanoAnalysisAll <- bind_rows(CorsanoAnalysisCombined, CorsanoAnalysisBoth) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA)) %>%
  arrange(Subject, Week, Time)

# Clean up the original split dataframe as well
CorsanoAnalysissplit <- CorsanoAnalysissplit %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), replace_nan_with_NA))

# --- Export Processed Data ---
export_list <- list(
  CorsanoAnalysissplit = CorsanoAnalysissplit,
  CorsanoAnalysisAll = CorsanoAnalysisAll
)

for (file_name in names(export_list)) {
  path <- file.path(valid_path, "Outputs", paste0(file_name, ".xlsx"))
  write.xlsx(export_list[[file_name]], path, rowNames = FALSE)
}



#**================================================================**
#** 4. Main Cosinor Analysis & Statistics Calculation Loop        **
#**================================================================**

# --- Initialization ---
# Define subjects to process, excluding any already completed
subjectnames <- unique(CorsanoAnalysissplit$Subject)

# Use one 'processed_subjects' list for simplicity
if (!exists("processed_subjects1")) processed_subjects1 <- character()
subjectnames <- setdiff(subjectnames, processed_subjects1)

# Initialize lists to store results efficiently
CorsanoAnalysisWave_list <- list()
Stattmp_list <- list()

# --- Main Processing Loop ---
for (subject in subjectnames) {
  cat("Processing Patient:", subject, "\n")
  
  # Create subject-specific output folder
  subject_folder <- file.path(valid_path, "Graphs", subject)
  if (!dir.exists(subject_folder)) {
    dir.create(subject_folder, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Process for "Weekday", "Weekend", and "Both"
  weekz <- c("Weekday", "Weekend", "Both")
  
  for (dayz in weekz) {
    cat("  Processing period:", dayz, "\n")
    
    # Filter data for the current analysis scope
    if (dayz == "Both") {
      GLMMSplit <- filter(CorsanoAnalysissplit, Subject == subject)
    } else {
      GLMMSplit <- filter(CorsanoAnalysissplit, Subject == subject, Week == dayz)
    }
    
    # Skip if there's insufficient data
    if (nrow(GLMMSplit) < 70) {
      cat("    Skipping due to insufficient data (", nrow(GLMMSplit), " rows).\n")
      next
    }
    
    Wavedatatmp_list <- list()
    
    # --- Loop through each biomarker to perform cosinor analysis ---
    for (bio in biolist) {
      
      # Ensure the biomarker column has enough data
      if (sum(!is.na(GLMMSplit[[bio]])) < 10) next
      
      # Run GLMM Cosinor Analysis (wrapped in tryCatch to handle model errors)
      model_formula <- as.formula(paste(bio, "~ amp_acro(time_col = 'Time', period = c(24, 12), n_components = 2)"))
      
      SplitModel2 <- tryCatch({
        cglmm(model_formula, data = GLMMSplit)
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("    ERROR fitting model for", bio, ":", e$message, "\n")
        return(NULL)
      })
      
      if (is.null(SplitModel2)) next
      
      # --- Generate predictions and summarize ---
      prediction <- predict(SplitModel2, GLMMSplit)
      Wavedatatmp1 <- GLMMSplit[, c("Time", bio)]
      Wavedatatmp1[[paste0(bio, "Cosine")]] <- prediction
      
      # Summarize raw data and cosine predictions
      Wavedatatmp1 <- Wavedatatmp1 %>%
        group_by(Time) %>%
        summarise(
          !!bio := mean(!!sym(bio), na.rm = TRUE),
          !!paste0(bio, "SEM") := sd(!!sym(bio), na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(!!sym(bio)))),
          !!paste0(bio, "Cosine") := mean(!!sym(paste0(bio, "Cosine")), na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = 'drop'
        )
      
      Wavedatatmp_list[[bio]] <- Wavedatatmp1
    } # End biomarker loop
    
    # --- Consolidate and Export Results for the subject/week ---
    if (length(Wavedatatmp_list) > 0) {
      # Combine all biomarker dataframes for this subject/week
      Wavedata <- Reduce(function(x, y) full_join(x, y, by = "Time"), Wavedatatmp_list)
      
      # Create 48-hour data for plotting
      Wavedata <- bind_rows(
        Wavedata,
        Wavedata %>% filter(Time != 0) %>% mutate(Time = Time + 24)
      ) %>% arrange(Time)
      
      # --- Export to Excel ---
      export_path <- file.path(subject_folder, paste0(subject, "_", dayz, "_Wave.xlsx"))
      write.xlsx(Wavedata, export_path)
      
      # --- Calculate Statistics (Min, Max, Amp, Mesor, etc.) ---
      cosine_data <- select(Wavedata, Time, ends_with("Cosine"))
      
      for (bio in biolist) {
        col_name <- paste0(bio, "Cosine")
        if (!col_name %in% names(cosine_data)) next
        
        vec <- cosine_data[[col_name]]
        
        if(all(is.na(vec))) next

        max_val <- max(vec, na.rm = TRUE)
        min_val <- min(vec, na.rm = TRUE)
        
        test_long <- data.frame(
          Patient = subject,
          week = dayz,
          Bio = bio,
          Amplitude = (max_val - min_val) / 2,
          Mesor = mean(vec, na.rm = TRUE),
          PPhase = cosine_data$Time[which.max(vec)],
          TPhase = cosine_data$Time[which.min(vec)],
          Max = max_val,
          Min = min_val
        )
        Stattmp_list[[length(Stattmp_list) + 1]] <- test_long
      }
      
      # Append collected wave data to the main list
      Wavedatatmp3 <- cosine_data %>%
          mutate(Subject = subject, Week = dayz)
      CorsanoAnalysisWave_list[[length(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list) + 1]] <- Wavedatatmp3
    }
    
  } # End dayz loop
  
  # Add subject to processed list after all its periods are complete
  processed_subjects1 <- c(processed_subjects1, subject)
  
} # End subject loop

#**================================================================**
#** 5. Final Aggregation and Export of Statistics                 **
#**================================================================**

# Combine all results from the lists at once for maximum efficiency
if (length(Stattmp_list) > 0) {
  Stattmp <- bind_rows(Stattmp_list)
  
  # Bind with any existing Stat data
  if(exists("Stat") && is.data.frame(Stat)) {
     Stat <- bind_rows(Stat, Stattmp)
  } else {
     Stat <- Stattmp
  }

  # Load and join patient demographic data if it exists
  patient_info_path <- file.path(valid_path, "Documentations", "patients.xlsx")
  if (file.exists(patient_info_path)) {
    PT <- read.xlsx(patient_info_path)
    Stat <- left_join(Stat, PT, by = c("Patient" = "Patient.Code"))
  }
  
  # Final arrangement and export
  Stat <- Stat %>%
    select(any_of(c("BMI", "week", "Bio", "Patient", "gender", "age")), everything()) %>%
    filter(Patient != "S5U469YF") %>%
    distinct()
 
  
  export_path <- file.path(valid_path, "Stats", "Full_Statistics_Optimized.xlsx")
  write.xlsx(Stat, export_path, rowNames = FALSE)
  cat("Statistical analysis complete. Results saved to:", export_path, "\n")
}

if (length(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list) > 0) {
  CorsanoAnalysisWave <- bind_rows(CorsanoAnalysisWave_list)
}

# Final cleanup
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), CoreDatasets))
```
